absent: Inner kmod config init and free helpers behavior beyond mutex framing.
Trigger run types and thread coordination semantics for driver versus filesystem tests.
Range update and integer display helper validation and formatting details.
Force init flag default and registration list and group table initial contents.
Lockup module parameter wiring and writability of controls after init.
High-priority workqueue ordering guarantees and CPU hotplug interaction during fan-out.
Page allocator flag interactions and mapping lifecycle for freed pages.
File open mode interactions and fput error handling beyond reference drop.
Maple tree bug-check handling and tree layout consequences of helpers.
Exact log message texts and rate-limit behavior.

findings.text: Test harness publishes one misc device per instance under dynamic minors with names built from test_kmod plus the numeric index and a sysfs group for configuration trigger reset and result inspection.

Load path registers a single test device and fails load when registration yields nothing. If a force-test control is active it then issues a driver run followed by a filesystem run, returning the first failure flagged by the warning helper.

Unload path walks the global device list safely under the registration lock, detaches each entry and then tears down its interface and storage. Teardown stops active tests while holding trigger then configuration locks, logs removal, unregisters the misc interface, releases locks in reverse order and frees storage.

Lockup test entry records the caller as main task, translates letters S D K R into sleeping versus running wait states with R selecting running, validates supplied lock addresses and optional magic values, refuses combinations that would sleep while atomic primitives are held, optionally opens a file to derive lock addresses, then either fans work to every online CPU or runs once locally, finally reporting timing and allocation failures and returning retry status unless interrupted.

Device attribute table exposes eight entries for trigger_config config reset config_test_driver config_test_fs config_num_threads config_test_case and test_result terminated by null. Case updates are bounded to valid identifiers excluding sentinels while reads report stored values.

Registration serializes with a global mutex, rejects creation when the device count would reach the maximum integer value, allocates indexed storage, registers a misc device and on success links the device into a global list, announces readiness and increments the count. Any registration failure frees the allocated storage and returns nothing.

Configuration initialization takes the per-device configuration mutex around the inner init helper. Allocation initializes three per-device mutexes for configuration trigger and thread control plus a completion for thread termination. Removal nests trigger outside configuration, and global list mutation nests the registration mutex outside per-device teardown.

Per-device state bundles a configuration block, three mutexes for configuration trigger and thread coordination, a completion signalling thread finish, an integer index, an embedded misc device with dynamic minor and generated name, a back pointer to the created device object and a list node linking it into the global registry.

Lifecycle progresses from zeroed allocation through mutex and completion setup and config bring-up, naming and misc registration, list publication, optional triggered runs, then on removal test stop, misc deregistration and staged freeing of name, auxiliary info, config and the container itself.
Timing controls start at zero for run and cooldown seconds and nanoseconds, one iteration, running state letter, disabled hrtimer and IO wait marking, and empty file path.

Lock and allocation controls default to read mode off, single-master mode off, reacquire off, watchdog touches off, conditional reschedule off, wait measurement off with maximal threshold, interrupt softirq preempt and RCU capture off, mmap and inode mapping and unmount capture off, zero lock addresses and page counts, kernel allocation flags with atomic override off, reallocation off and zeroed failure and peak atomics.

Acquisition order is mutex then semaphore then memory-map lock, followed by interrupt softirq preempt and RCU captures, then spinlock and read-write lock, with address-based and mmap locks taken only by the designated master while low-level captures apply to every participant. Release reverses that order. Read versus write mode follows a shared flag. Optional timing records peak acquisition latency with a compare-exchange loop and rate-limited reporting when a threshold is exceeded.

Each worker announces start, acquires selected locks, preallocates requested pages, then loops up to the iteration bound unless the main task shows a pending signal. Each pass marks IO wait optionally, waits the run interval, optionally frees pages, optionally drops locks, optionally touches watchdogs and yields, waits the cooldown interval, then optionally reacquires locks and reallocates pages. Finish logs elapsed time, frees pages and releases locks.

Wait in running state busy-delays for seconds and nanoseconds portions and returns. In sleeping states it sets the current sleep state and then either sleeps on a relative high-resolution timer built from seconds plus nanoseconds or sleeps on jiffies converted from the same split.

When fan-out is requested the initializer locks online-CPU membership, records the current CPU as master, initializes one work item per online CPU and queues each item on its CPU via the high-priority workqueue, then flushes every item before unlocking. Otherwise it runs directly as master. Per-CPU function treats the caller as master when single-master mode is off or when its work item matches the recorded master CPU.

Supplied lock addresses are rejected when they alias user space or when either endpoint fails a fault-free kernel read. Under spinlock debugging optional magic fields at type-specific offsets are checked against expected constants. Initialization also requires a memory context when mmap locking is requested and requires a file path when inode mapping or unmount locking is requested, deriving the semaphore address from the opened file structures.

Lock addresses supplied as unsigned numbers are cast to kernel lock types without ownership tracking, so a stale or wrong address can corrupt unrelated state. Sleeping waits combined with atomic captures are refused at init, but misconfiguration outside the checked combinations or concurrent mutation of controls could still place a sleep inside an atomic region.

Maple test shims wrap insert erase load store and range variants with kernel allocation flags, encode an index into a value for index tests and assert expected values on erase. Status helpers report none overflow and underflow from a state field. Range allocation checks invoke forward and reverse allocators and assert both return code and resulting position, returning early when an error code is expected.
Maple allocation test upper bound equals 0x2000000000000Ul.
Maple 32-bit indicator is true when node slot count exceeds 31.

Tree dump validation cache shrink and state dump helpers expand to empty statements, as do non-kernel marking and allocation-count reset helpers, while run and pass tallies are atomic counters. Maple search test configuration is enabled.
Device-count overflow guard tests exact equality against maximum integer after increment, so unexpected count mutation outside the registration lock could bypass the intended limit.
File control bundles a file pointer plus a cached inode pointer and a fixed 256 byte path buffer used to select inode mapping or superblock locks.
Maple helpers treat any unexpected return value position or loaded value as a fatal tree bug check, so erroneous test expectations halt rather than report soft failure.
Lockup logs prefix every message with the module name.
